variants.title: Move a job through its states
variants.context: A long generation leaves the synchronous path. The API admits an immutable contract, the scheduler routes compatible work, a worker produces a candidate, release policy inspects it, and delivery publishes durably. The state machine records exactly where the job stopped.
variants.prompt: A tenant submits a high-resolution generation. Put the five system boundaries in order.

items.text: Generate a candidate: encode conditioning, initialize latent noise from a seed, run the denoising passes, and decode pixels.
Schedule compatible work by model, precision, adapter, dimensions, priority, and memory class.
Admit the request: authenticate, normalize the prompt, enforce quota and policy, validate dimensions, and store one immutable contract.
Inspect and attest: evaluate the actual output, apply product policy, and record decision evidence.
Publish durably: store the asset and metadata, create a scoped URL, and complete the job with a stable output identifier.

variants.hint: Which boundary is the only one that can refuse work before it costs anything?
variants.explanation: Admission prevents invalid work, the GPU worker produces a candidate, and release policy decides whether that candidate may leave the system.

variants.title: Move a job through its states
variants.context: A long generation leaves the synchronous path. The API admits an immutable contract, the scheduler routes compatible work, a worker produces a candidate, release policy inspects it, and delivery publishes durably. The state machine records exactly where the job stopped.
variants.prompt: A job succeeds on its first attempt. Put its recorded states in order.

items.text: Record moderating once pixels exist but are not yet releasable.
Record succeeded once an accepted asset and its evidence are durable.
Record queued once a scheduler owns the request, priority, and deadline.
Record accepted once the contract and idempotency key are durable.
Record running once one worker lease owns the current attempt.

variants.hint: Pixels existing is its own state, not the end of the job.
variants.explanation: Explicit states let a client retry with the same idempotency key return the existing job instead of buying another generation.

variants.title: Move a job through its states
variants.context: A long generation leaves the synchronous path. The API admits an immutable contract, the scheduler routes compatible work, a worker produces a candidate, release policy inspects it, and delivery publishes durably. The state machine records exactly where the job stopped.
variants.prompt: A candidate fails the output gate. Put the states in order, ending at the terminal reason.

items.text: Record queued while the job waits with its deadline and priority.
Record running while the worker lease produces pixels.
Record moderating while the pixels exist and no release decision has been made.
Record rejected with a terminal reason that is safe to query.
Record accepted with the release policy that will apply to this contract.

variants.hint: The policy that decides this job was chosen long before the pixels appeared.
variants.explanation: Terminal reasons are recorded and queryable, so a rejection is an auditable outcome rather than a missing result.

variants.title: Schedule and reconcile
variants.context: A scheduler builds batches from jobs that can actually share a loaded worker. It classifies the job from the immutable contract, picks a compatible queue, leases a warm worker with a deadline and heartbeat, then reconciles the attempt before any retry.
variants.prompt: A job is dispatched to a GPU pool for the first time. Put the scheduling steps in order.

items.text: Choose a compatible queue that separates interactive, batch, and review-sensitive work and preserves tenant fairness.
Reconcile the attempt by committing output identity atomically with attempt state.
Lease a worker that already has the required recipe loaded, with a deadline, heartbeat, cancellation token, and stable job ID.
Derive model family, memory class, dimensions, quality tier, deadline, and policy route from the immutable contract.

variants.hint: Compatibility is decided from the contract, not discovered on the worker.
variants.explanation: Mixing incompatible models, adapters, dimensions, or precision modes creates reload churn and unpredictable memory pressure.

variants.title: Schedule and reconcile
variants.context: A scheduler builds batches from jobs that can actually share a loaded worker. It classifies the job from the immutable contract, picks a compatible queue, leases a warm worker with a deadline and heartbeat, then reconciles the attempt before any retry.
variants.prompt: A lease expires while the job may or may not have produced an accepted output. Put the recovery steps in order.

items.text: Commit the new output identity atomically with the attempt state.
Mark the attempt expired once the heartbeat stops.
Retry on a compatible worker only when no accepted output was found, inside the attempt budget.
Check whether an accepted output already exists for this job identity.

variants.explanation: Expired leases may be retried only after checking whether an accepted output already exists, which is what prevents duplicate publication.

variants.title: Schedule and reconcile
variants.context: A scheduler builds batches from jobs that can actually share a loaded worker. It classifies the job from the immutable contract, picks a compatible queue, leases a warm worker with a deadline and heartbeat, then reconciles the attempt before any retry.
variants.prompt: Scale-down selects a worker to drain. Put the drain steps in order.

items.text: Remove the worker so stale capacity is not trapped in the pool forever.
Let bounded in-flight work finish inside its existing deadline.
Release the loaded model and return its capacity to the pool accounting.
Stop granting new leases to that worker.

variants.hint: Draining is about what stops first, not about what is killed.
variants.explanation: Scale-down must stop new leases, allow bounded in-flight work to finish, and preserve loaded-model economics without trapping stale capacity.

variants.title: Size the pool
variants.context: Keep job seconds, measured images per minute, utilization, and queue age as separate numbers. Utilization is arrival rate divided by capacity, and denoising work grows roughly with spatial area times denoising passes times image count.
variants.prompt: A worker pool is measured at 25 images per minute. Requests arrive at 20 images per minute. What is the modeled utilization before retry and burst headroom?
variants.hint: Utilization is a ratio, not a difference.
variants.explanation: Utilization is arrival rate divided by capacity, and it stays a separate number from job seconds and queue age.

mistakes.feedback: You divided capacity by arrivals; utilization is arrivals over capacity.
You subtracted the two rates instead of dividing them.

variants.title: Size the pool
variants.context: Keep job seconds, measured images per minute, utilization, and queue age as separate numbers. Utilization is arrival rate divided by capacity, and denoising work grows roughly with spatial area times denoising passes times image count.
variants.prompt: A profile generating one image at 512 by 512 is changed to 1024 by 1024 with the same denoising passes and image count. By what factor does the modeled denoising work grow?
variants.hint: Denoising work follows spatial area, not one side.
variants.explanation: Work grows roughly with spatial area times denoising passes times image count, and doubling both sides quadruples the area.

mistakes.feedback: You scaled one dimension; area grows with width and height together.
You squared the area factor, which already accounts for both dimensions.

variants.title: Size the pool
variants.context: Keep job seconds, measured images per minute, utilization, and queue age as separate numbers. Utilization is arrival rate divided by capacity, and denoising work grows roughly with spatial area times denoising passes times image count.
variants.prompt: Requests arrive at 48 images per minute and the team wants to run at a target utilization of 0.8. What measured capacity does the pool need?
variants.hint: Target utilization is the fraction of capacity you intend to use.
variants.explanation: Capacity is arrival rate divided by target utilization, which is what leaves headroom for retries and heterogeneous jobs.

mistakes.feedback: You multiplied by the target utilization instead of dividing by it.
That runs the pool at full utilization and leaves no headroom for retries or bursts.

variants.title: Reject at admission
variants.context: Admission control exists so invalid or unbounded work never reaches a queue. Dimensions, references, adapters, the work estimate, and the release policy are all decided before generation starts.
variants.prompt: A tenant requests an aspect ratio that no worker pool in the selected model family supports. What should the API do?
options: Accept it and silently round the dimensions to the nearest supported shape.
Reject the request at admission with an explicit reason instead of queueing it.
Queue it and let the first worker that dequeues it report the incompatibility.
optionFeedback: Wrong: silently changing the contract produces an image the caller did not ask for and cannot audit.
Correct: dimensions must match the selected model and worker pool constraints before the job is queued.
Wrong: a queue is not a substitute for admission control, and the failure surfaces after the wait.
variants.hint: A queue is not a substitute for admission control.
variants.explanation: Invalid combinations are rejected at admission, so a caller learns immediately and no GPU capacity is reserved for impossible work.

variants.title: Reject at admission
variants.context: Admission control exists so invalid or unbounded work never reaches a queue. Dimensions, references, adapters, the work estimate, and the release policy are all decided before generation starts.
variants.prompt: A team wants to pick the release policy after seeing whether the generated image looks risky. What is wrong with that?
options: Release policy must be selected before work starts, not inferred after a surprising image appears.
Nothing, as long as the strictest available policy is then applied to every candidate.
Nothing, because the output gate sees the pixels and the prompt gate does not.
optionFeedback: Correct: policy version, required checks, audience, retention, and review route belong to the immutable contract.
Wrong: a policy chosen after the fact cannot be audited, and required checks may already have been skipped.
Wrong: the output gate applies a policy; it does not get to choose which policy the job was under.
variants.hint: Which part of the contract has to be immutable?
variants.explanation: The contract fixes the release policy before generation, so the release decision and its evidence can be audited later.

variants.title: Reject at admission
variants.context: Admission control exists so invalid or unbounded work never reaches a queue. Dimensions, references, adapters, the work estimate, and the release policy are all decided before generation starts.
variants.prompt: A request attaches a reference image with no stated purpose, no size bound, and no retention rule. What should admission do?
options: Accept it but strip the reference before generation so the job stays bounded.
Reject it until the purpose is authorized and its size and retention are bounded.
Accept it and apply the default retention used for generated output assets.
optionFeedback: Wrong: stripping the reference silently changes the intent the caller submitted.
Correct: a reference asset needs an authorized purpose, a bounded size, and a known retention rule.
Wrong: a default meant for generated output does not establish an authorized purpose for user-supplied input.
variants.hint: What must the contract say about an input the system will store?
variants.explanation: Reference assets carry rights and retention consequences, so admission rejects them until purpose, size, and retention are explicit.

variants.title: Sort the parts
variants.context: The generation contract separates intent, render envelope, model recipe, and release policy, and each failure mode has a designed behavior. Naming the part is what makes an incident explainable instead of a guess about the model.
variants.prompt: A design review splits one request into contract parts. Match each part with the fields it holds.

pairs.label: Intent
pairs.detail: Prompt, negative constraints, reference assets, requested operation, and locale.

pairs.label: Render envelope
pairs.detail: Width, height, image count, quality tier, deadline, priority, and maximum spend.

pairs.label: Model recipe
pairs.detail: Model and encoder versions, adapters, sampler, steps, guidance, precision, and seed policy.

pairs.label: Release policy
pairs.detail: Policy version, required checks, audience, retention, provenance mode, and review route.

variants.hint: One part is user-controlled and one is infrastructure that can change under the user.
variants.explanation: Separating intent from envelope, recipe, and policy is what lets infrastructure change without rewriting what the user asked for.

variants.title: Sort the parts
variants.context: The generation contract separates intent, render envelope, model recipe, and release policy, and each failure mode has a designed behavior. Naming the part is what makes an incident explainable instead of a guess about the model.
variants.prompt: A launch review lists four failures. Match each failure with the behavior the system is supposed to have.

pairs.label: Worker dies mid-job
pairs.detail: Mark the attempt expired, reconcile any committed output, and retry within the attempt budget.

pairs.label: Moderation is unavailable
pairs.detail: Hold or fail closed for policies that require the missing check.

pairs.label: Object storage fails
pairs.detail: Keep the job nonterminal and delete orphaned temporary pixels through a reconciler.

pairs.label: Callback delivery fails
pairs.detail: Keep the job queryable and retry signed callbacks without rerunning generation.

variants.hint: Only one of these should ever cause the model to run again.
variants.explanation: Failure behavior is designed before launch so a notification gap never becomes a second expensive generation.

variants.title: Sort the parts
variants.context: The generation contract separates intent, render envelope, model recipe, and release policy, and each failure mode has a designed behavior. Naming the part is what makes an incident explainable instead of a guess about the model.
variants.prompt: An autoscaler is being tuned. Match each pressure signal with what it actually reveals.

pairs.label: Oldest runnable job age
pairs.detail: How far a tier already is from its service objective.

pairs.label: Estimated queued GPU seconds
pairs.detail: How much work is waiting inside one compatibility class.

pairs.label: Warm-worker ratio and model-load duration
pairs.detail: How much of a new job's latency is model loading.

pairs.label: Out-of-memory and retry rates
pairs.detail: Whether the batch shape or memory class is misjudged.

pairs.label: Sustained utilization
pairs.detail: Whether one worker failure would still leave enough capacity.

variants.hint: Autoscale from pressure, not from CPU.
variants.explanation: Each signal answers a different question, which is why a single utilization number cannot decide when to add or drain a worker.
